briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for November 5, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and the Urgency of Adaptation
sections.content: Recent reports indicate that the impact of the climate crisis on daily life is growing, as seen in the 'out-of-season mosquito' attacks due to extreme weather phenomena [9] and the surge in home insurance premiums in Georgia [8]. In particular, climate change adversely affects ecosystems such as trout [54], and rising sea levels exacerbate coastal flooding and storm surges, increasing casualties and property damage [58]. Furthermore, climate change is harming our health [55, 72], placing the heaviest burden particularly on women [55], and affecting how children grow [65], thereby causing severe ripple effects across society. The UN has warned that COP30 adaptation pledges will be woefully insufficient for the needs of developing countries [62], pointing out that these countries require $305 billion annually for climate change adaptation but face a shortfall of $277 billion [70]. In response, the President of the European Central Bank urged the Eurozone to adapt more quickly to climate change [61], and the pioneering role of Dr. Mayer Hillman, who warned about climate change ahead of his time, is being re-examined [75].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Carbon Neutrality Transition Efforts and Innovations
sections.content: Domestically, various public-private partnerships and innovative attempts are continuing to achieve carbon neutrality. Following the launch of the Geomdan-gu Climate Crisis Response Committee [5, 13], Gyeongnam Province and Seodaemun-gu are encouraging citizen participation through carbon neutrality education and the development of game-based environmental map puzzles [11, 15]. Companies are also responding to the climate crisis through science and technology-based innovations, such as developing climate-adaptive barley for beer [2], alternative crops using grape seeds and jujube seeds [4], and lab-grown chocolate and coffee [69]. In the construction sector, Korea's first 10-story wooden apartment building is set to be utilized as a carbon neutrality experimental site [12], while Buyeo-gun and Chungnam Province are expanding infrastructure to accelerate carbon neutrality through the completion of hydrogen fueling stations [23, 25]. Internationally, climate response efforts utilizing technology are active, with Ai2, supported by Google, undertaking a project to transform AI weather models into climate change prediction tools [56]. These efforts are spreading across culture and society, including the Hanji exhibition at the Wonju Climate Change Promotion Center [1] and KCC Glass's disclosure of ESG management performance [6] [20, 22, 26, 31, 71].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Policy Shifts and the Pursuit of Cooperation
sections.content: Recent U.S. midterm elections, with the Democratic Party gaining control of Congress, are expected to positively influence climate and clean energy policies [7, 53, 57, 63]. Experts analyze that this 'blue wave' will have significant implications for climate action [53, 57]. Internationally, with the COP31 UN Climate Summit approaching [50, 64], concrete discussions for climate action are progressing, including Brazil's announcement of a global 'roadmap' as COP30 president to end deforestation and transition away from fossil fuels [77, 78]. Furthermore, the progress in GEPA discussions among Korea, Singapore, and New Zealand [3] and the emphasis on carbon neutrality technology cooperation with Chinese networks in industrial and economic sectors [30] suggest the importance of establishing international trade directions for climate change response and technological collaboration. The European Union (EU) is pushing to withdraw 'green claims' and implementing 'eco-friendly and carbon-neutral' advertising regulations [18] to enhance the credibility of environmental claims, while the WHO emphasized the importance of concrete actions, stating that just six climate actions could save 1.6 million lives annually [68]. Domestically, efforts to address climate change are also active in policy and academic fields, with Seoul Metropolitan Council member Kim Jeong-hee delivering a special lecture on 'The AI Era and Carbon Neutrality' [16, 27], and Jungwon University hosting a carbon neutrality response meeting [29] [28, 66, 67].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Market Trends
sections.content: The renewable energy sector is accelerating its growth globally, creating new investment and business opportunities. The Democratic Party's control of the U.S. Congress has raised expectations for policy benefits in the renewable energy industry, leading to a simultaneous rise in related stocks [36, 39, 44, 47]. Domestically and internationally, concrete efforts to expand renewable energy are continuing, including investment plans for solar and onshore wind power [37, 41], the selection of Bonghwa-gun for the rural RE100 project [42], and the projected growth of the superconducting cable market due to grid modernization and renewable energy integration [43]. Vietnam and Indonesia have ample room for cooperation in renewable energy and green city development [48], and Samsung C&T is also actively engaged in international cooperation and investment, discussing infrastructure and renewable energy projects [32] [33, 34, 38, 40, 45, 46]. Amidst these positive trends, however, COP31 host country Turkey is showing a 'two-faced' approach, expanding renewable energy while also ranking first in Europe for coal power [35], and the possibility of the government prematurely ending tax exemptions for eco-friendly buses has been raised [49], revealing the complexities and challenges of the decarbonization transition. Particularly, the increasing power demand from data centers is highlighted as a significant challenge for carbon neutrality [24], indicating a situation that requires continuous attention and policy support.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted both the severity of the climate crisis, global response efforts, and the hopeful trends in renewable energy transition. This is a critical time when comprehensive efforts and international cooperation are more vital than ever for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
